reason: Both answers say don't match, lock in the base with term commitments, discount only selectively, move upmarket or niche down, and counter-position against VC subsidy. A adds a concrete calculation of what a 40% cut costs ($1.2M ARR, about $100k a month) and a fenced stripped-down tier for head-to-head deals, which makes the targeted-response point more actionable. B adds burn reduction and a 30–60 day wait-and-measure step, but these are marginal and the wait sits a little awkwardly with acting on renewals now. A is slightly stronger.
